LICENSE declares AGPLv3 and conditional linking additional permission for independent modules under approved licenses. This partial source research selects neither a license/distribution strategy nor an unpatched upstream kernel binary.

Current handle_oom transfers two kernel-quota pages from a source PD to destination; a prefer-source policy can fall back to core. If transfers fail it requests remote memory revocation and compares reported usage. Continued failure returns PD_OOM; comments describe deferred RCU release. The OOM handler initializes UPGRADE_CORE_TO_DST and commonly chooses core as donor even for non-core interactions. Success resumes original IPC; unresolved OOM blocks on a semaphore. STOP and unknown-case paths exist. No deadline or global frozen total is established by these paths.

Each inspected helper retries its operation while PD_OOM and OOM handling returns OK. VM helper explicitly requests a core-to-target upgrade. There is no explicit iteration cap or elapsed deadline in these loops. This is a source-level absence of a finite local bound, not proof that an actual invocation hangs or consumes unbounded physical memory.

PD creation passes literals for two pages kept unavailable for upgrades and32 upper-limit pages. Invalid selector and create failure are logged/returned as coded. Destruction invokes revoke then removes the capability mapping; flush revokes a flexpage sequence. These callsites do not establish syscall completion deadlines or full resource release. In light of upgrade paths,32 is not an established fixed lifetime or whole-subsystem maximum; kernel implementation and patch semantics remain outside this receipt.

VM construction wraps RAM/cap quota guards, trace control, heap and memory-map owners, withdraws one cap and creates the VM PD with the same2/32 parameters. vCPU startup, portal mapping, EC/semaphore creation and memory delegation use upgrade helpers, including a VMM-PD target. Mapping failures return allocation/invalid-dataspace classifications. RAM and capability guards do not independently attest a nonexpanding kernel quota or all external backing costs.

VM destruction iterates and destroys vCPUs; vCPU destructor dissolves entrypoint identity, removes trace source and replenishes/removes its cap range. PD-selector destructor removes its mapping with revoke semantics delegated to unseen implementation. Detach invokes revocation over flexpages. Pager destruction revokes cleanup/block portals. Member/base destructors, cap-map implementation, kernel RCU, all VMM/device/provider lifetimes and partial-constructor unwind need additional source closure; these nine files are not a full cleanup proof.
